title: Solar Photovoltaic Installers

bls.growth: 37 percent projected 2025-2035, much faster than average

summary: PV installers build, wire and maintain solar electric systems, mostly on rooftops, and connect them to the building and the grid. The work mixes roofing and racking carpentry, DC and AC wiring, testing and labeling. Heights and sunlight-energized DC circuits are the two defining hazards.
typicalPath: BLS: a high school diploma or equivalent, then roughly one month to a year of on-the-job training; technical school or community college courses are optional. Licensing is required in some states, and NABCEP certification is optional but required by some states for subsidized projects. In practice a licensed electrician often performs or supervises the electrical portion; this varies by state and was not confirmed in the pages opened. Source: BLS OOH page above.

tasks.task: Install PV systems following applicable codes and standards.
tasks.electricalKnowledge: NEC 690, 705, 250, 110 and the adopted local amendments

tasks.task: Check wiring, polarity and grounding continuity of installed arrays.
tasks.electricalKnowledge: Meter use, polarity and ground continuity testing, NEC 690.43 and 250

tasks.task: Identify electrical, environmental and other safety hazards before and during the job.
tasks.electricalKnowledge: Shock and DC arc hazards, energized-by-light arrays, fall hazards

tasks.task: Judge array location, orientation and structural suitability of the roof or site.
tasks.electricalKnowledge: Site survey, shading, roof condition, fire-code setbacks

tasks.task: Assemble modules and support or racking structures.
tasks.electricalKnowledge: Listed racking that also bonds modules (UL 2703), mechanical attachment

tasks.task: Seal roof penetrations and arrays against weather.
tasks.electricalKnowledge: Mostly roofing practice; not an NEC topic

tasks.task: Run interconnecting wiring, with the means to disable it safely.
tasks.electricalKnowledge: PV wire and connectors, conductor sizing, rapid shutdown (690.12), wiring methods

tasks.task: Label system components with required identification and warnings.
tasks.electricalKnowledge: NEC 690 and 705 marking, rapid shutdown labels, max DC voltage marking

tasks.task: Draw array layouts and site features for the installation.
Plan materials and the sequence of installation steps.
Connect inverters, combiners and disconnects to the building electrical system.
tasks.electricalKnowledge: NEC 705 load-side and supply-side connections, overcurrent protection, disconnects

tasks.task: Commission systems, record readings and hand off to inspector and utility.
tasks.electricalKnowledge: Voc, Isc, polarity, insulation resistance tests; interconnection paperwork

tasks.task: Work at height on roofs and ladders using fall protection, in a team.
tasks.importance: context: 69 percent regularly exposed to high places

procedures.name: Site survey and roof fall protection
procedures.purpose: Assess the roof and site, then keep workers from falling during array installation.
procedures.whenUsed: Whenever work is at 6 feet or more above a lower level, which includes essentially all rooftop PV work.
procedures.role: Every crew member; the employer provides systems and training.
steps: Review plans and permit conditions and the adopted fire-code setbacks.
Walk the roof and check condition, slope, decking and attachment points.
Locate the service panel, meter, conduit routes and shading sources.
Identify overhead power lines, skylights, and roof edges and openings.
Inspect harness, lanyard or rope grab and connectors before use.
Install anchors into structural members, not sheathing alone.
Set ladder at a safe angle, secure it and extend it above the roof edge.
Connect to the anchor before stepping onto the roof.
Use guardrails or a safety monitor where the plan calls for them.
Keep tools and modules from sliding off the roof.
hazards: Slips on wet or dusty roofs
controls: Personal fall arrest systems, guardrails or monitored warning lines per OSHA
Ladder securing and three points of contact

standards.name: OSHA 29 CFR 1926.501(b)
standards.what: Roof workers at 6 feet or more need guardrails, nets, fall arrest or permitted alternatives.

standards.name: OSHA 29 CFR 1926.502
standards.what: Defines performance of guardrails, nets and arrest systems, such as 42-inch top rail and 6-foot free-fall limit.

standards.name: International Fire Code section 1205 / IRC R324
standards.what: Sets rooftop access pathways and ridge setbacks; exact distances depend on adopted edition and amendments.

evidence.says: Fall protection is required at 6 feet on low-slope and steep roofs, with allowed system choices.
Gives system criteria: guardrail height and strength, net placement, arrest force and free-fall limits.
Solar crews typically use harness and retractable lanyard; ladder setup and securing are stressed.
Setbacks and pathways vary by adopted edition and local amendment; the AHJ decides.

procedures.appCoverage: partial: the app now teaches the sequence and the safety reasoning through a skill lesson and a step-by-step practice of the procedure; it has no hands-on tool or simulation for it. (Before wave 1 the rating was: none: no height-work content; this is OSHA safety, not an NEC skill.)
procedures.appCoverageBefore: none: no height-work content; this is OSHA safety, not an NEC skill.

procedures.name: Array installation, DC wiring and connector handling
procedures.purpose: Mount modules and wire strings with listed, correctly mated connectors and protected conductors.
procedures.whenUsed: During the main install phase after racking is set.
procedures.role: PV installers, with an electrician where state rules require.
steps: Set racking and attach modules per manufacturer instructions.
Cover or keep modules shaded when practical while wiring.
Mate connectors of the same listed type and check they are fully seated.
Route and secure PV wire and cable so it is protected from damage and abrasion.
Label and group strings as shown on the single-line diagram.
Run DC circuits in the approved wiring method to the combiner or inverter.
Seal roof penetrations and confirm conduit and box fittings.
Verify all work against the plan set before closing up.
hazards: DC arc from damaged or loose connectors
controls: Matched connectors and torque to manufacturer values
Module covering or shading while connecting

standards.name: NEC Article 690 (Parts IV and others)
standards.what: Wiring methods, conductor and connector requirements and listed equipment for PV circuits; wording is edition-sensitive.

standards.name: NEC Article 110
standards.what: General installation rules such as workmanship and equipment suitability.

standards.name: NEC 705.11 connectors/splices (as summarized in source)
standards.what: Connectors and splices must suit the conductor and ampacity, installed per manufacturer.

evidence.says: PV components must be listed or evaluated; metal parts connect to the equipment grounding conductor.
PV arrays cannot be de-energized in light; DC arcs sustain; gloves and testing practices apply.
Summarizes 2023 NEC points on connectors, torque and listed components.

procedures.appCoverage: partial: the sandbox teaches AC panel wiring and conductor choices, but not DC strings, connectors or PV wire.

procedures.name: Inverter, combiner, disconnect and rapid shutdown installation
procedures.purpose: Place and connect conversion and shutdown equipment so the array can be isolated and firefighters are protected.
steps: Mount inverter and combiner in a code-compliant, accessible location per listing.
Install the PV disconnecting means and any required AC disconnect.
Install rapid shutdown devices or listed system components per manufacturer.
Wire the initiating device where the system needs one and place it per plan.
Connect overcurrent protection sized from the design.
Apply required rapid shutdown and warning labels.
Test the shutdown function and record the result.
hazards: Shock from DC and AC terminals
controls: Rapid shutdown limiting controlled conductors to low voltage within a set time
Listed shutdown equipment used per instructions

standards.name: NEC 690.12
standards.what: Requires rapid shutdown of PV conductors on buildings; limits and methods changed in 2017, 2020 and 2023 editions.

standards.name: UL 3741
standards.what: Product safety standard for PV hazard control systems, referenced from NEC 2020 and 2023.

standards.name: NEC 690.13-690.15
standards.what: Disconnecting means and isolation requirements for PV equipment (section numbers recalled; not opened).

evidence.says: Describes how rapid shutdown limits changed across 2017, 2020, 2023 NEC and the role of UL 3741 and initiation devices.
Lists equipment listing, disconnect and plaque duties and where PV equipment may not be installed.

procedures.appCoverage: partial: disconnecting means and overcurrent skills transfer to the AC side, but rapid shutdown and PV-specific equipment are not taught.

procedures.name: Grounding and bonding of the array
procedures.purpose: Bond all exposed metal and provide a fault path so ground faults are detected and cleared.
procedures.whenUsed: During racking and wiring, and verified at commissioning.
steps: Use racking and bonding hardware listed for module bonding.
Bond module frames and rails per the hardware instructions.
Run the equipment grounding conductor from array to inverter and panel.
Size the EGC from the overcurrent device rating and protect small sizes from damage.
Connect any optional grounding electrode to the premises electrode system.
Confirm ground-fault protection is present in the inverter.
Test ground continuity before energizing.

standards.name: NEC 690.43 and Article 250
standards.what: Exposed metal PV parts must connect to the equipment grounding conductor using listed bonding means.

standards.name: UL 2703
standards.what: Listing for mounting systems that also bond modules.

evidence.says: Explains UL 2703 racking bonding, EGC routing, optional electrodes and DC ground-fault protection.
Metal frames connect to the EGC sized by Table 250.122; GFDI applies above stated thresholds.

procedures.appCoverage: partial: the earthing-bonding skill trains bonding and grounding concepts for buildings, not array bonding hardware or DC ground-fault protection.

procedures.name: Commissioning tests and electrically safe testing
procedures.purpose: Prove the installed system is correct and safe before energizing and handing over.
procedures.whenUsed: After installation, before inverter start-up and utility permission.
procedures.role: Installer or commissioning technician, often two people.
steps: Visually inspect wiring, labels, grounding and mounting with the system off.
Check meter on a known source, test, then recheck the meter.
Test continuity of grounding conductors.
Check polarity of each string at the combiner.
Measure open-circuit voltage per string and compare with temperature-corrected expected values.
Measure short-circuit current per string where the procedure calls for it.
Test insulation resistance with the disconnects open.
Start the inverter per manufacturer steps and verify AC side and shutdown.
Record results in the commissioning report.
controls: Test sequence with polarity before connection

standards.name: NABCEP PV Installation Professional JTA
standards.what: Lists commissioning tasks: Voc, polarity, insulation resistance, Isc, labeling, interconnection.

standards.name: IEC 62446-1
standards.what: Outside the NEC; defines a PV test and documentation sequence commonly used as a reference.

standards.name: NFPA 70E
standards.what: Electrical safe work practices and PPE for energized testing; edition-sensitive (not opened).

evidence.says: Installation and commissioning domains include Voc, polarity, insulation resistance, Isc and labeling tasks.
Describes DC tests, expected Voc correction, insulation test with disconnects open and handover documents.
Recommends live-dead-live testing and rated PPE.

procedures.appCoverage: none: the app does not yet teach meter testing; no skill trains these steps.

procedures.name: Interconnection and utility hand-off
procedures.purpose: Connect the system to the building service and obtain utility permission to operate.
procedures.whenUsed: Design and permitting for the application; after inspection for permission to operate.
procedures.role: Installer company, electrician, inspector and the utility.
steps: Submit the interconnection application with equipment data.
Choose load-side or supply-side connection per panel limits.
Install the connection and the required plaque or directory at the service.
Obtain permit sign-off and pass the AHJ inspection.
Provide documents to the utility.
Wait for utility permission to operate before exporting.
Leave labels, as-builts and manuals for the owner.

standards.name: NEC Article 705
standards.what: Rules for connecting power sources in parallel with the utility, including supply-side and load-side taps.

standards.name: UL 1741 / IEEE 1547
standards.what: Inverter listing and grid interconnection performance including anti-islanding; outside the NEC.

standards.name: Utility interconnection tariff
standards.what: Utility-specific application, study and permission rules; varies by utility and state.

evidence.says: Four steps: application, permits, inspection, permission to operate; 120 percent rule and IEEE 1547 and UL 1741.
2023 NEC rewrote Article 705 including supply-side connections and added island mode and microgrid parts.

procedures.appCoverage: partial: load calculation and service concepts exist, but no source interconnection, 120 percent rule or utility process.

procedures.name: Battery storage installation
procedures.purpose: Install energy storage with correct disconnects, protection, location and shutdown.
steps: Confirm the unit is listed to UL 9540 and read its instructions.
Check allowed location and spacing with the fire code and AHJ.
Mount unit and install the lockable disconnect in sight or within the stated distance.
Size conductors and protection for continuous current.
Install the emergency shutdown device where required.
Label the system and apply any shock or arc warnings.
Commission and log maintenance records.

standards.name: NEC Article 706 and 480
standards.what: Electrical installation, disconnects, protection and labels for storage and batteries.

standards.name: NFPA 855 / IRC R328 / IFC
standards.what: Fire-code location, spacing and capacity limits for storage; outside the NEC and edition-sensitive.

standards.name: UL 9540 / 9540A
standards.what: Listing and fire test method for storage systems.

evidence.says: Summarizes 706 disconnect and label duties and NFPA 855 spacing and capacity limits.
2023 706.7 adds formal commissioning requirements for storage.
2023 NEC changed Articles 706 and 480 scope, commissioning and disconnects.

procedures.appCoverage: none: no batteries or storage content; skills touch only generic disconnect and location ideas.

standardsAndCodes.name: NEC Article 690 Solar Photovoltaic Systems
standardsAndCodes.role: Core PV rules: circuits, wiring, disconnects, rapid shutdown, grounding, arc-fault, labeling.

standardsAndCodes.name: NEC Article 705 Interconnected Power Production Sources
standardsAndCodes.role: Connecting the system to the service and parallel operation, plaques.

standardsAndCodes.name: NEC Article 706 Energy Storage Systems and 480 Stationary Batteries
NEC Article 710 Stand-Alone Systems
standardsAndCodes.role: Off-grid systems with no utility connection.

standardsAndCodes.name: NEC Article 691 Large-Scale PV Electric Supply Stations
standardsAndCodes.role: Utility-scale plants; rarely touched by residential installers.

standardsAndCodes.name: NEC Article 250 and 110
standardsAndCodes.role: Grounding and bonding and general installation requirements.

standardsAndCodes.name: OSHA 29 CFR 1926 Subparts M and K
standardsAndCodes.role: Fall protection and construction electrical safety including lockout and tagging (1926.417).

standardsAndCodes.name: UL 1741, UL 2703, UL 3741, UL 9540
standardsAndCodes.role: Product listings for inverters, racking and bonding, hazard control systems, storage.

standardsAndCodes.name: IEEE 1547 and utility interconnection rules
standardsAndCodes.role: Grid performance and the permission-to-operate process.

outsideNec: Fire-code roof access pathways and ridge setbacks (IFC section 1205, IRC R324) set by the adopted edition and local amendments.
Battery location, spacing and capacity limits (NFPA 855, IRC R328, IFC).
OSHA fall protection, ladders and construction electrical safety.
Structural and roofing work: attachment loads, flashing and weatherproofing.
UL product listings (1741, 2703, 3741, 9540) and IEC 62446-1 test practice.
Utility interconnection agreements, IEEE 1547 settings and permission to operate.
Contractor licensing and permit rules by state and AHJ.
gapsForTheApp: PV system skill family: array, string, combiner, inverter, rapid shutdown and DC conductors are not in the 13 skills.
Rapid shutdown: a skill and scenario teaching 690.12 and its edition differences.
Testing with a meter: Voc, polarity, insulation resistance and live-dead-live in a safe simulated array.
Roof and fall-protection scenario: site survey, anchors and setback layout in 3D.
Interconnection: 705 load-side and supply-side connections and the 120 percent rule using the panel sandbox.
Battery storage: 706 disconnects, emergency shutdown, labels and fire-code siting.
Edition awareness: content tagged by NEC and fire-code edition because 690, 705 and 706 changed in 2017, 2020 and 2023.
DC arc and lockout practice in construction: no lockout or energized-work content exists.
doubts: O*NET page summary did not show importance numbers for interconnection or commissioning tasks; I did not see the full task list directly.
NEC edition-specific section numbers (690.13 to 690.15, 705.11, 706.15) were not verified against NFPA text, which is paywalled; third-party summaries were used.
Fire-code setback distances: only secondary sources, and they conflict by edition; the source I opened said distances vary by adoption and amendment.
NEC 2026 changes to 690, 705 and 706 were not researched; sources cover 2017 to 2023 editions.
Two sources I tried (NREL PDFs, yakimacounty fire PDF) did not load or were unreadable; IEC 62446-1 preview did not load, so test order came from a search result summary plus a blog.
NFPA 70E specifics and Article 691 content were not opened.
Whether PV installers need an electrical license varies by state and was not confirmed.
OSHA 1910.147 excludes construction; the construction lockout rule I opened is 1926.417 (tagging), which is thinner than 1910.147.
The Battery storage and Site survey procedures have only two to three sources, mostly trade blogs rather than primary standards.
